root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: the retained barcode crop satisfies `w >= 100 && h >= 50` before width decoding continues.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `pixReadBarcodes()` forwards a retained deskewed barcode crop into `pixReadBarcodeWidths()`, the crop must satisfy the same minimum-size gate that the fixed program enforces: its width must be at least 100 pixels and its height at least 50 pixels. Shorter crops must not enter the raster-averaging path at all.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original forwards the accepted deskewed crop without any minimum-size check, so a 32-pixel-tall crop still reaches the fixed 51-scan averaging path. The fixed program inserts this size gate upstream and therefore guards the later `pixAverageRasterScans()` call on the original PoC.

nodes.state: At the marked first-row read, `i < 0`, so `line = data + i * wpl` points before the first raster row and `GET_DATA_BYTE(line, j)` reads outside the barcode crop. AddressSanitizer reports that this out-of-range byte lands inside the temporary `pixe` allocation already freed by `pixLocateBarcodes()`.

edges.relation: The same retained deskewed barcode crop that misses the upstream size gate in `pixReadBarcodes()` is forwarded unchanged through `pixReadBarcodeWidths()` into `pixAverageRasterScans()`.

The negative `first` row index derived for the short-image window is reused unchanged as the loop index at the first marked read, carrying the before-buffer row selection directly into `GET_DATA_BYTE`.
